LESSON: READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.1 Reading Fluency (2 sessions) • Reading speed • Intonation • Particle
Topic 2.3: Reading for Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading for Comprehension, part of Reading 2.1 Reading Fluency (2 sessions) • Reading speed • Intonation • Particle in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can you extract specific information from a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read a short text fluently and at a good pace,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. respond to questions from a text based on the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read a short text fluently and at a good pace,

   Reading for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. respond to questions from a text based on the theme,

   Reading for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.

   Reading for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to read a short text on animals fluently,

2. collaborate with peers to conduct a speed reading game and identify the best speed to read at,

3. peer assess each other’s performance for fluency,

4. work jointly to respond to direct and inferential questions from the texts read.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to read a short text on animals fluently,
2. collaborate with peers to conduct a speed reading game and identify the best speed to read at,
3. peer assess each other’s performance for fluency,
4. work jointly to respond to direct and inferential questions from the texts read.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading for Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner is motivated to learn continually when conducting a speed reading game

and identifying the best speed to read.

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is enhanced as the learner follows simple instructions to respond to direct and

inferential questions from the texts read.

Values:
Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to assess each other’s performance for fluency.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Animal welfare: This is promoted as the learner identifies and appreciates different animals and birds found in their locality.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate this concept to similar concepts about birds and animals covered in Agriculture.
